transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Evan Marshall (Thornwood Head of Platform), Lena Ortiz (VP Eng), Rahul Mehta (Security), Sofia Kim (SRE)

[00:00:05] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our systems SE. Quick check, you all can hear us?
[00:00:12] Evan: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks.
[00:00:15] Priya: Hi team. We'll do a quick discovery so we can scope Dedicated capacity for Thornwood. Short agenda: current infra, workloads, isolation needs, burst patterns, and POC asks.
[00:00:27] Lena: Sounds good. We're mostly focused on replacing a lot of our internal LLM endpoints that currently run on k8s with GPUs. Need isolation for sensitive customer PII and predictable tail latency during market hours.
[00:00:38] Jordan: Great. Can you give a bit of context — current model usage, QPS, peak concurrency, and any on-prem constraints?
[00:00:46] Evan: Sure. Right now we have mixed usage. Day trading desk stuff is high priority during US market open 9:30-16:00, so we see spikes in inference requests. Typical baseline is around 150 qps for embeddings and small generation calls, peak bursts up to 1,200 concurrent tokens-ish during big replays. We also run large batch jobs overnight for risk recalcs, those can soak GPUs for hours.
[00:01:12] Sofia: To add, the latency SLO for the trading front-end is 200 ms p95. If it slips we get alerts.
[00:01:20] Priya: Okay that latency target is doable but it affects sizing and batching. Are you currently using any KV caching or prefix caching?
[00:01:28] Lena: We have a homegrown cache but it's inconsistent. Some model endpoints maintain short lived KV cache per session. I think we could benefit from Redwood's automatic prefix/K-V cache, whatever you call it.
[00:01:40] Jordan: Yeah, our runtime supports KV cache and prefix cache; it helps a lot with repeated context. For Dedicated we can pin instances to guarantee locality of cache for a customer.
[00:01:49] Rahul: On the security side: we require SOC two report, encryption at rest with our KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk. Also SSO/SCIM for user access. Do you support those in Private or Dedicated?
[00:02:02] Priya: We do. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs. For hosted we have options but Dedicated gives better isolation. Our control plane can integrate with SAML SSO and SCIM.
[00:02:12] Rahul: Good. We also have a strict requirement around data residency for EU customers — some subsets must never leave EU. How does Redwood route requests by region?
[00:02:21] Jordan: We have region-aware routing policies. With Dedicated you can provision capacity in a specific region and pin model versions to that cluster. If you need stricter on-prem we have Redwood Private, which is a different engagement.
[00:02:33] Evan: Cost is important. We like the predictability of reserved capacity but worried about underutilization. How do you handle burst? Can Dedicated burst to hosted?
[00:02:42] Priya: Yep — Dedicated can be configured with burst policies. You can reserve a base GPU pool and allow controlled burst to our hosted fleet during emergencies or scheduled peaks. There's a policy layer where you set priority, max burst, and fallback model variants. If you want absolute isolation with no external network calls, that's where Private comes in.
[00:03:00] Lena: For many of our workloads we could accept burst to hosted for non-sensitive models, but the trading front-end must stay within Dedicated or Private. So we need routing per-route.
[00:03:10] Priya: That's supported. You can tag routes as 'sensitive' and keep them pinned. Non-sensitive routes can have fallback to hosted or cheaper quantized variants.
[00:03:20] Evan: On quantization — we've been talking about q8_0 vs q4, aware that more aggressive quant gets cheaper but might reduce quality. Does Redwood help recommend quantization profiles?
[00:03:30] Jordan: Redwood Optimize includes model and quantization recommendations by workload. For Dedicated we can run evals on your prompts and suggest a config that balances quality vs tokens cost. Priya, we often run small eval suites, right?
[00:03:40] Priya: Yup. We'll provide a benchmark template; send us representative prompts, we'll run them on a few candidate quant profiles and share latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
[00:03:50] Rahul: Need to confirm KMS — customer-managed means keys in our cloud KMS (GCP/AWS) and Redwood can access them via cross-account roles?
[00:03:58] Priya: Exactly. We support cross-account KMS integration and can do HSM-backed keys for Private deployments if needed.
[00:04:07] Sofia: For scaling, are you using autoscaling within the Dedicated pool? We have diurnal load — high during market hours, low overnight, then large batch jobs.
[00:04:16] Priya: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and scheduled scaling. You can define target utilization, min/max pool, and scheduled boosters for known heavy windows. For batch heavy jobs we recommend using burst capacity or separate batch-only pools so they don't evict low-latency front-end instances.
[00:04:33] Evan: If we set up a batch pool, can it share model artifacts to reduce cold-starts?
[00:04:38] Priya: Yes — model artifacts and KV cache can be shared on-cluster. We manage model versioning and pinning to reduce warm-up latency.
[00:04:46] Lena: One of our constraints is predictable tail latency p95 — can you provide guarantees?
[00:04:51] Jordan: Our Dedicated SLAs include latency targets for provisioned profiles. We'll include specifics in the SLA doc. For guaranteed p95 you'll want reserved capacity sized to handle your peak concurrency.
[00:05:02] Priya: Also you'll want to tune batching off for those ultra-low latency routes, or set small max-batch windows. There's a tradeoff: batching increases throughput but can add a few ms.
[00:05:11] Evan: What about observability? We need per-token cost breakdowns and traces.
[00:05:16] Jordan: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can forward traces to your APM too.
[00:05:24] Rahul: Any compliance gotchas with audit logs? For example, are admin actions logged with user identifiers?
[00:05:29] Priya: Yes — audit logs include user and token IDs, and we retain logs per your retention policy. We'll work with you on retention, export, and encryption standards.
[00:05:39] Evan: For the POC, what would you typically recommend? One of our high-priority routes, mirrored traffic for a week, run benchmarks and then a 2-week pilot?
[00:05:48] Priya: Typical POC: a small Dedicated pool sized for baseline + measured burst patterns, run mirrored traffic for 3–7 days, run synthetic benchmarks for 24–48 hours, and then evaluate. We can do a cost projection and provide rollback strategies.
[00:06:01] Lena: Mirror traffic might be heavy — what's the ingestion pattern? We might only mirror a subset.
[00:06:06] Jordan: Mirroring a subset is fine. Start with a representative subset of users or routes. We'll also need your telemetry to size correctly.
[00:06:14] Evan: Ok, on sizing — here's some rough numbers: baseline 150 qps, peak 1,200 concurrent small requests, average 40 tokens per request for gen calls, embeddings are lighter but more frequent. Can you ballpark GPUs?
[00:06:27] Priya: Ballpark only: for these numbers depending on model size, maybe 4–8 x A100 or equivalent for baseline, with burst pool of another 4 GPUs. But we'll need to run benchmark with your payload to be precise. If you use quantized 7B-ish models you might need fewer.
[00:06:42] Rahul: Do you support mixed GPU types in a pool? We have access to some on-prem A30s too.
[00:06:48] Priya: You can have mixed pools but scheduler will route by compatibility. For consistent latency it's recommended to use homogeneous pools. Mixed is possible for cost optimization.
[00:06:58] Lena: One more: how do upgrades/rollouts work? We need canary deploys and immediate rollback if regressions.
[00:07:05] Jordan: Rollouts support canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies, and you can pin client traffic. The console shows regressions and we can tie quality regressions to eval prompts.
[00:07:16] Evan: Are there any gotchas for connecting our internal VPC — NATs, private endpoints, etc?
[00:07:21] Priya: For Dedicated we typically provision in your VPC with private endpoints. We'll do peering or transit gateway depending on cloud. For Private on-prem we package the runtime. We'll share the network diagram in the security packet.
[00:07:33] Rahul: Perfect. Please include the network diagram and exact firewall rules.
[00:07:37] Jordan: We'll include that in the security doc pack.
[00:07:40] Evan: Timeline — we want a pilot before end of Q2 if possible. Internal approvals pending.
[00:07:45] Jordan: Good, that seems feasible. We'll get pricing for a Dedicated baseline + burst options and an estimated pilot cost.
[00:07:52] Lena: On the pricing note, do you price by GPU-hour or effective token cost?
[00:07:57] Jordan: For Dedicated it's a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual) with GPU-hour pricing plus support. We also provide per-token accounting so you can see unit economics. Burst to hosted is charged per usage.
[00:08:10] Sofia: Any limits on model variants? We want to run a couple of Llama-based and a closed-source model.
[00:08:16] Priya: We support a catalog of open models and can onboard custom models. For closed-source you can bring your own model binary; we validate compatibility.
[00:08:24] Rahul: Final question — can you do a short perf test during pilot with our real payload, including encrypt-by-client-key flows?
[00:08:31] Priya: Yes, we can run perf tests using your encrypted payloads; we'll need key exchange for KMS access setup.
[00:08:38] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps...
[00:08:41] Jordan: Action items: I'll send pricing/SLA, Priya will share benchmarks and configs, Evan will send traffic telemetry, Rahul will send compliance docs, and we'll schedule follow-up technical deep dive.
[00:08:55] Evan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:08:58] Lena: Thanks, talk soon.

[End of recording — transcription may include minor mis-hearings, e.g., "Redwood Dedi" instead of Redwood Dedicated, "K-V" vs KV cache, "SOC two" for SOC2.]
